segments.title: HMS Africa remembered in song
segments.summary: A short musical tribute portrays HMS Africa as an old 64-gun ship that keeps going as shot and shell fall around her.
segments.body: This two-minute special replaces a conventional ship history with a celebratory song. The lyrics place HMS Africa amid war drums, quiet conversation below decks, eight bells, moonlight, and a sailor's reassurance that she will not give up. The refrain has shot and shell raining down, yet the old 64-gun ship keeps going and arrives in time to do what she must. Calling her a mighty goddess turns the warship into an object of affection and loyalty.

evidence.note: The song repeatedly names HMS Africa, describes shell and shot falling on her, and identifies her as an old 64-gun ship.

segments.title: HMS Africa and the Trafalgar videos
segments.summary: The closing remarks explain why HMS Africa received the song and direct viewers to the Trafalgar videos for a fuller account.
segments.body: After the song, HMS Africa is called a very, very cool ship that deserved the tribute. Viewers are directed to a link below for more about her in the Trafalgar videos. The performance ends with a self-deprecating joke about being a flat bass and probably never singing another special. This closing minute connects the song to the channel's longer treatment of the battle.

evidence.note: Dr. Clarke describes HMS Africa as a very cool ship and directs viewers to the Trafalgar videos through a link below.
